neighbours.label: the bare piece ' b' opening a lowercase word that the tokenizer splits (b|anded, b|imodal, b|asking); not b-words that are one token or that open with another piece
fire: Each autumn the wardens caught and banded several hundred young terns.
The survey found a bimodal pattern in the lengths of the fish.
In warm regions this butterfly is bivoltine and flies twice a year.
The tortoise spends the morning on its basking rock near the pond.
The mud samples were rich in benthic worms and small clams.
A herd of bison grazed on the far side of the river.
Rare mosses grow in the bogs on the northern slope.
The mower left neat rows of bales across the hay field.
quiet: Each autumn the wardens caught and tagged several hundred young terns.
The survey found a broad pattern in the lengths of the fish.
In warm regions this butterfly is biennial and flies every second year.
The tortoise spends the morning on its favourite rock near the pond.
The mud samples were rich in brackish worms and small clams.
A herd of brown cattle grazed on the far side of the river.
Rare mosses grow in the bracken on the northern slope.
The mower left neat rows of barley across the hay field.

notes: The top examples also hold ' B' opening a split capitalised name and a few medical tokens; a probe read 0.60 on ' and' in 'laser, vitrectomy and injections'. The + pole peaks on ' B' too.
